title: Typography, Colors & Backgrounds
description: Transform plain text into beautiful reading experiences. Master web fonts, typographic scale, color systems, gradients, and background techniques that make designs feel polished and professional.
learningObjectives: Load and apply web fonts using @font-face and Google Fonts
Build a typographic scale with rem units
Work with color formats: hex, rgb, hsl, oklch
Control backgrounds: images, size, position, multiple layers

sections.content: 🎯 Use rem units for font sizes (relative to root, not parent). Use unitless line-height so it scales proportionally with font size.

exercises.question: Why should you use unitless values for line-height (e.g., 1.5 instead of 24px)?
options: It scales proportionally with any font-size
It is required by the CSS spec
It only works with rem fonts
exercises.correctAnswer: It scales proportionally with any font-size
hints: What happens to 24px line-height on a 32px heading vs a 14px caption?
exercises.explanation: Unitless line-height (like 1.5) multiplies the current font-size. 1.5 on a 32px heading gives 48px line-height. On a 14px caption it gives 21px. A fixed 24px would be too tight on the heading and too loose on small text.

lessons.title: Color Systems: hex, rgb, hsl, oklch

sections.content: 🎯 Use HSL for design systems — you can create a full palette by keeping H fixed and varying L: hsl(239, 84%, 95%) for the lightest shade, hsl(239, 84%, 30%) for the darkest.

exercises.question: In HSL color notation hsl(0, 100%, 50%), what color is this?
hints: H=0 means the first hue on the color wheel
exercises.explanation: H=0 (or 360) is red on the color wheel. S=100% means fully saturated (vivid). L=50% is the mid-point — pure red.

sections.content: Gradients are images in CSS — they can be used anywhere an image is accepted: background, background-image, border-image, mask. No image file needed.

exercises.question: Which CSS function would you use to create a pie chart effect with CSS only?
hints: It sweeps around a center point like a clock
exercises.explanation: conic-gradient() sweeps color stops around a center point (like pie slices). Combine with border-radius: 50% to create a circular pie chart.

exercises.question: Which background-size value fills the container completely, potentially cropping the image?
hints: It 'covers' every pixel of the container
exercises.explanation: cover scales the image to completely cover the container. If the aspect ratios differ, the image is cropped. contain scales to fit within the container — no cropping but may leave empty space.

sections.content: 🎯 Use clamp() for fluid typography that scales smoothly between mobile and desktop without breakpoints.

exercises.question: What does clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem) do to font-size?
options: Scales between 1rem and 2rem based on viewport width
exercises.correctAnswer: Scales between 1rem and 2rem based on viewport width
exercises.explanation: clamp() returns the preferred value (2.5vw) clamped between min (1rem) and max (2rem). On small screens it won't go below 1rem; on large screens it won't exceed 2rem.

capstoneProject.title: Blog Typography System
capstoneProject.description: Build a beautiful blog article page using only the concepts from this module — a professional typographic system, a color palette in HSL, gradient headers, and styled background sections.
requirements: Load two Google Fonts (one for headings, one for body)
Define a complete typographic scale using CSS variables (xs through 4xl)
Build a full HSL-based color palette (5 shades of primary color)
Gradient hero section using linear-gradient over a background image
Gradient text effect on the article title using background-clip
Fluid h1 using clamp() for responsive sizing
Truncated article summaries with multiline ellipsis
